UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user's profile within the Visionary app.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user profile.

profilePicture.description: URL of the user's profile picture.

visionScore.description: Overall vision score calculated from tests.

preferences.description: User preferences, stored as a JSON string.

EyeTest.title: EyeTest
EyeTest.description: Represents a single eye test taken by a user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the eye test.

testType.description: The type of eye test (e.g., Visual Acuity, Color Vision).

testDate.description: Date and time the test was taken.

results.description: JSON string containing the detailed test results.

Workout.title: Workout
Workout.description: Represents a guided eye workout or exercise routine.

name.description: Name of the workout routine (e.g., Morning Focus).

description.description: Description of the workout and its benefits.

exercises.description: JSON string containing the sequence of exercises in the workout.

duration.description: Total duration of the workout in minutes.

category.description: Category of the workout (e.g., Focus, Strain Relief).

UserWorkout.title: UserWorkout
UserWorkout.description: Represents a workout performed by a user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user workout.

completionDate.description: Date and time the workout was completed.

performanceData.description: JSON string containing detailed performance data for the workout.

Reminder.title: Reminder
Reminder.description: Represents a reminder for eye exercises or medication.

reminderTime.description: Time of day for the reminder.

repeatDays.description: JSON string containing an array of days the reminder should repeat.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure is designed to ensure security, scalability, and debuggability, aligning with the principles of Authorization Independence, Clarity of Intent, DBAC (Database-Based Access Control), and QAPs (Rules are not Filters). Authorization Independence is achieved through denormalization, specifically by avoiding `get()` calls in security rules. This is crucial for maintaining atomic operations and simplifying debugging.  The structure supports the required QAPs by using structural segregation and path-based ownership.

*   **UserProfile**: User profiles are stored in a path-based structure under `/users/{userId}`. This ensures private data is securely accessible only to the authenticated user.
*   **EyeTest, Workout, UserWorkout, Reminder**: These entities are also structured under `/users/{userId}`, maintaining the path-based ownership and simplifying security rules based on user ID.  This approach ensures that listing eye tests, workouts, user workouts and reminders is secure because the rules can simply check `request.auth.uid == userId` without the need to filter based on data within the documents.
*   **Workouts** are stored in `/workouts/{workoutId}`.  These are global resources, accessible to all users, but write access would typically be restricted to administrative roles (not defined in the schema, but assumed for the application to function).
